hook.convey: factor = a number that divides exactly (12 laddoos in equal lines on a tray: 3 lines of 4 or 4 lines of 3, none left); multiple = in the number's times table (balls bowled after 1, 2, 3 overs of 6 balls) → factors are few, multiples go on forever

use.hi: Cricket mein ek over mein 6 ball hoti hain. 1 over ke baad 6 ball, 2 over ke baad 12, 3 over ke baad 18. Yeh 6 ke multiples hain, aur match chalta rahe toh yeh list badhti hi jaati hai.
use.en: In cricket an over has 6 balls. After 1 over, 6 balls; after 2 overs, 12; after 3 overs, 18. These are multiples of 6, and as long as the match goes on, the list keeps growing.

use.hi: Kitchen mein 12 laddoo ek tray mein barabar lines mein rakhne hain. 3 lines mein 4-4 rakh sakte ho, ya 4 lines mein 3-3, ek bhi laddoo nahi bachta. Isliye 3 aur 4 dono 12 ke factors hain.
use.en: In the kitchen, 12 laddoos go on a tray in equal lines. You can put 4 in each of 3 lines, or 3 in each of 4 lines, with not one laddoo left over. So 3 and 4 are both factors of 12.

explain.convey: factor = divides the number exactly, remainder 0 → 12 tiles laid as a rectangle, 3 rows and 4 columns, none left → 3 and 4 are factors of 12; the same tiles in another rectangle give another factor pair

point.hi: Yeh 12 tiles hain, 3 rows aur 4 columns mein, ek bhi tile bachi nahi. 12 ko 3 se bhaag do toh poora 4 aata hai, shesh 0. Factor woh number hai jisse 12 poora-poora bhaag ho jaaye, isliye 3 aur 4 dono 12 ke factors hain.
point.en: These are 12 tiles, in 3 rows and 4 columns, with not one tile left over. Divide 12 by 3 and you get exactly 4, remainder 0. A factor is a number that divides 12 exactly, so 3 and 4 are both factors of 12.

prompt.hi: Inhi 12 tiles ko 2 rows mein barabar lagao. Har row mein kitni tiles aayengi?
prompt.en: Lay these same 12 tiles in 2 equal rows. How many tiles go in each row?

why.hi: 12 ÷ 2 = 6, aur ek bhi tile nahi bachti
why.en: 12 ÷ 2 = 6, with not one tile left over

simpler.hi: 12 tiles 3 rows mein 4-4 karke lag gayi, ek bhi nahi bachi. Jo number 12 ko bina kuch bachaye baant de, woh 12 ka factor hai.
simpler.en: The 12 tiles fit in 3 rows of 4, with none left over. A number that shares 12 with nothing left over is a factor of 12.

explain.convey: list factors in pairs starting from 1 → 16 = 1 × 16, 2 × 8, 4 × 4 → both numbers of every pair are factors, so 1 and the number itself always belong; 4 × 4 gives 4 only once → the child counts the factors of 16

point.hi: 16 ki factor ki jodiyan dekho: 1 × 16, 2 × 8 aur 4 × 4. Jodiyan hamesha 1 se shuru karo. Har jodi ke dono numbers 16 ke factors hain, isliye 1 aur khud 16 bhi factor hain; har number ke liye 1 aur woh number khud hamesha factor hote hain. 4 × 4 mein 4 ek hi baar ginte hain.
point.en: Look at the factor pairs of 16: 1 × 16, 2 × 8 and 4 × 4. Always start the pairs from 1. Both numbers of every pair are factors of 16, so 1 and 16 itself are factors too; for every number, 1 and the number itself are always factors. In 4 × 4, the 4 is counted only once.

prompt.hi: Toh 16 ke kul kitne factors hain?
prompt.en: So how many factors does 16 have in all?

why.hi: 16 ki jodiyan 1, 2, 4, 8 aur 16 deti hain, 1 aur 16 hamesha; 4 ek hi baar, yaani 5 factors
why.en: the pairs give 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16, so 5 factors, with the 4 counted only once

simpler.hi: 16 ko do numbers ke guna se banao: 1 × 16, 2 × 8, 4 × 4. Har jodi ke dono numbers factor hain, bas 4 ko ek hi baar gino.
simpler.en: Make 16 as two numbers multiplied: 1 × 16, 2 × 8, 4 × 4. Both numbers of each pair are factors; just count the 4 once.

explain.convey: multiples = the number's times table → hops of 4 from 0 land on 4, 8, 12 and keep going → the list never ends; factors are at most the number itself, multiples start at it and grow → the child picks the multiple of 4 from a small and a big number

point.hi: Number line par 0 se 4-4 ki chhalaang lagao: 4, 8, 12. Yeh 4 ke multiples hain, yaani 4 ke pahade ke numbers. Chhalaang lagaate raho toh yeh list kabhi khatam nahi hoti. Factor 4 ko poora bhaag karta hai aur 4 se bada nahi hota, par multiple 4 se shuru hokar badhta hi jaata hai.
point.en: On the number line, hop 4 at a time from 0: 4, 8, 12. These are multiples of 4, the numbers in the 4 times table. Keep hopping and this list never ends. A factor divides 4 exactly and is never bigger than 4, but a multiple starts at 4 and keeps growing.

prompt.hi: Inhi chhalaangon ke hisaab se, 2 ya 20, inmein se 4 ka multiple kaunsa hai?
prompt.en: Going by these hops, which of 2 or 20 is a multiple of 4?

why.hi: 20 = 4 × 5, toh 20 4 ke pahade mein hai, par 2 toh 4 se bhi chhota hai
why.en: 20 = 4 × 5, so 20 is in the 4 times table, but 2 is even smaller than 4

simpler.hi: 4 ke multiples 4 ke pahade mein aate hain: 4, 8, 12, aur aage. Koi bhi multiple 4 se chhota nahi hota.
simpler.en: Multiples of 4 are the numbers in the 4 times table: 4, 8, 12 and on. No multiple is smaller than 4.

problem.hi: 28 ke saare factors batao, aur 28 ke pehle paanch multiples bhi batao.
problem.en: List all the factors of 28, and also the first five multiples of 28.

simpler.hi: Do kaam hain. Pehle jodiyan banakar 28 ke factors. Phir 28 ka pahada, paanch tak.
simpler.en: There are two jobs. First the factors of 28, by making pairs. Then the 28 table, up to five.

find.hi: 28 ke saare factors aur 28 ke pehle paanch multiples
find.en: all the factors of 28 and the first five multiples of 28

do.hi: 28 ki factor ki jodiyan 1 se shuru karke dhoondo
do.en: Find the factor pairs of 28, starting from 1

why.hi: 3, 5 aur 6 se 28 poora bhaag nahi hota, shesh bachta hai
why.en: 3, 5 and 6 do not divide 28 exactly; a remainder is left

simpler.hi: 28 ko 1 se shuru karke chhote numbers se bhaag do. Jo poora bhaag de, uski jodi likho, jaise 2 × 14.
simpler.en: Divide 28 by small numbers, starting from 1. When one divides exactly, write its pair, like 2 × 14.

steps.result: 7 pehle hi 4 × 7 mein aa chuka, jodiyan poori

why.hi: ab jodiyan ulti hokar dohraayengi, naya factor nahi milega
why.en: the pairs would now repeat in reverse, so no new factor will come

simpler.hi: 7 toh 4 × 7 wali jodi mein pehle hi aa gaya. Ab jodiyan ulti dohrayengi, isliye yahin ruk jao.
simpler.en: 7 is already in the pair 4 × 7. From here the pairs just repeat backwards, so stop here.

do.hi: Jodiyon ke saare numbers chhote se bade kram mein likho
do.en: Write all the numbers of the pairs from smallest to biggest

why.hi: har jodi ke dono numbers factor hain, 1 aur 28 bhi
why.en: both numbers of every pair are factors, 1 and 28 too

simpler.hi: Saari jodiyon ke numbers ek line mein chhote se bade likho. Har jodi ke dono numbers factor hain, 1 aur 28 bhi.
simpler.en: Write the numbers from all the pairs in one line, smallest to biggest. Both numbers of each pair are factors, 1 and 28 too.

do.hi: Ab 28 ko 1, 2, 3 aur 4 se guna karo

why.hi: multiple 28 ke pahade mein aata hai
why.en: a multiple is in the 28 times table

simpler.hi: 28 ka pahada bolo: 28 × 1, 28 × 2, aur aage. Har jawab 28 ka ek multiple hai.
simpler.en: Say the 28 times table: 28 × 1, 28 × 2 and on. Each answer is a multiple of 28.

prompt.hi: Paanchwa multiple, yaani 28 × 5, kitna hai?
prompt.en: The fifth multiple, that is 28 × 5, is how much?

simpler.hi: Pichhla multiple 112 tha. Usmein ek baar aur 28 jod do.
simpler.en: The last multiple was 112. Add one more 28 to it.

why.hi: 2 × 14 jaisi jodiyan factors deti hain; multiples 28, 56, 84, 112 ke baad 28 × 5 = 140
why.en: pairs like 2 × 14 give the factors; the multiples go 28, 56, 84, 112, then 28 × 5 = 140

answer.hi: 28 ke factors 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 aur 28 hain, aur pehle paanch multiples 28, 56, 84, 112 aur 140 hain
answer.en: the factors of 28 are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 and 28, and the first five multiples are 28, 56, 84, 112 and 140

why.hi: factor 28 ko poora bhaag karta hai isliye list 28 par rukti hai, par multiples ka pahada kabhi khatam nahi hota
why.en: a factor divides 28 exactly, so the list stops at 28, but the multiples are the 28 times table, which never ends

prompt.hi: 30 tiles 5 rows aur 6 columns mein lagi hain. {friend} kehta hai 30 ke factors 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15 hain. Usne kaunse do factors chhod diye?
prompt.en: 30 tiles are laid in 5 rows and 6 columns. {friend} says the factors of 30 are 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15. Which two factors did he leave out?

why.hi: 30 ki sabse pehli jodi 1 × 30 hai, aur wahi chhoot gayi
why.en: the very first pair of 30 is 1 × 30, and that is the one left out

simpler.hi: 30 ki jodiyan 1 se shuru karke likho, jaise 5 × 6. Phir dekho, har jodi ke dono numbers us list mein hain ya nahi.
simpler.en: Write the pairs of 30 starting from 1, like 5 × 6. Then see whether both numbers of every pair are in that list.

prompt.hi: {friend} kehta hai ki 27, 9 ka factor hai, kyunki 27 = 9 × 3. Kya {friend} sahi hai?
prompt.en: {friend} says 27 is a factor of 9, because 27 = 9 × 3. Is {friend} right?

why.hi: 27 = 9 × 3, toh 27, 9 ka multiple hai; 9 ke factors sirf 1, 3 aur 9 hain
why.en: 27 = 9 × 3, so 27 is a multiple of 9; the factors of 9 are only 1, 3 and 9

simpler.hi: Factor 9 ko poora bhaag deta hai, isliye woh 9 se bada nahi hota. Ab dekho 27, 9 se bada hai ya chhota.
simpler.en: A factor divides 9 exactly, so it is never bigger than 9. Now see whether 27 is bigger or smaller than 9.

prompt.hi: 8 tiles 2 rows aur 4 columns mein lagi hain. 1, 8 ya 16, inmein se kaunsa number 8 ka factor bhi hai aur multiple bhi?
prompt.en: 8 tiles are laid in 2 rows and 4 columns. Which of 1, 8 or 16 is both a factor of 8 and a multiple of 8?

why.hi: 8 khud ko poora bhaag karta hai aur 8 × 1 = 8 hai; 1 multiple nahi, 16 factor nahi
why.en: 8 divides itself exactly and 8 × 1 = 8; 1 is not a multiple, 16 is not a factor

simpler.hi: Factor is number ko poora bhaag deta hai, aur multiple iske pahade mein aata hai. Teeno options ko dono baaton par parkho.
simpler.en: A factor divides this number exactly, and a multiple is in its times table. Test all the options against both rules.

say.en: The small numbers that divide 12 exactly, like 3 and 4, are factors of 12, numbers inside 12. Now look at the hops of 12 on the number line: they land on multiples of 12, and these multiples never end.

simpler.hi: 3 aur 4 se 12 poora bhaag hota hai, isliye woh 12 ke factors hain. 12-12 ki chhalaang 12 ke multiples par utarti hai, jo badhte hi jaate hain.
simpler.en: 3 and 4 divide 12 exactly, so they are factors of 12. Hops of 12 land on multiples of 12, which keep on growing.

prompt.hi: Board par 0 se 12-12 ki chhalaang hai. 6 ya 48, inmein se 12 ka factor kaunsa hai?
prompt.en: The board shows hops of 12 from 0. Which of 6 or 48 is a factor of 12?

why.hi: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 poora aata hai, par 48 = 12 × 4 toh 12 ka multiple hai, factor nahi
why.en: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 exactly, but 48 = 12 × 4 is a multiple of 12, not a factor

simpler.hi: Factor 12 ko poora bhaag deta hai, isliye woh 12 se bada nahi ho sakta. Dekho 48, 12 se bada hai ya chhota.
simpler.en: A factor divides 12 exactly, so it cannot be bigger than 12. See whether 48 is bigger or smaller than 12.

remediation.move: factor pairs as a rainbow from 1: 18 = 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6 → the first pair is 1 with the number itself, so both ends are always in the list; ask who 1's partner is

say.hi: Jodiyan hamesha 1 se shuru karo. Pehli jodi hoti hai 1 guna khud woh number, isliye 1 aur woh number dono factors ki list mein aate hain. Har jodi ke dono numbers gino.
say.en: Always start the pairs from 1. The first pair is 1 times the number itself, so 1 and the number are both in the list of factors. Count both numbers of every pair.

simpler.hi: Pehli jodi hamesha 1 guna woh number hoti hai. Isliye 1 aur khud woh number bhi factor hain.
simpler.en: The first pair is always 1 times the number. So 1 and the number itself are factors too.

prompt.hi: 14 ki jodiyan 1 × 14 aur 2 × 7 hain. 14 ke kul kitne factors hain?
prompt.en: The pairs of 14 are 1 × 14 and 2 × 7. How many factors does 14 have in all?

why.hi: dono jodiyon se 1, 2, 7 aur 14, yaani 4 factors milte hain
why.en: the two pairs give 1, 2, 7 and 14, so 4 factors

simpler.hi: Har jodi ke dono numbers 14 ke factor hain. Dono jodiyon ke numbers ek list mein likho aur gino.
simpler.en: Both numbers of each pair are factors of 14. Write the numbers from both pairs in one list and count them.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tum ek number ke factors aur multiples nikaal sakte ho. Agle hisse mein do numbers ke factors ki listein milayenge aur dekhenge kaunse factors dono mein hain.
bridgeToNext.en: Now you can find the factors and multiples of one number. In the next part we will put the factor lists of two numbers side by side and see which factors are in both.

simpler.hi: Ab do numbers ke factors ki listein saath rakhkar dekhenge. Board par 15 aur 25 ke factors ki listein hain.
simpler.en: Now we put the factor lists of two numbers side by side. On the board are the factor lists of 15 and 25.

hook.convey: two amounts shared into the same equal groups with nothing left → the number of groups must divide both → a common factor; 1 is in every list, so two numbers always share at least 1

use.hi: School ke paas 12 cricket bat aur 18 ball hain. Inse ek jaisi kits banani hain, koi bat ya ball bachni nahi chahiye. Kitni kits banengi, yeh 12 aur 18 dono ke factors se tay hota hai.
use.en: A school has 12 cricket bats and 18 balls. It wants to make identical kits from them, with no bat or ball left over. How many kits can be made is decided by the factors of both 12 and 18.

use.hi: Kitchen mein 8 roti aur 12 kebab barabar plates mein lagane hain, har plate ek jaisi. Plates ki ginti aisi ho jo 8 ko bhi poora bhaag kare aur 12 ko bhi.
use.en: In the kitchen, 8 rotis and 12 kebabs go onto equal plates, every plate the same. The number of plates must divide 8 exactly and divide 12 exactly too.

explain.convey: common factor = in the factor list of both numbers → 15: 1, 3, 5, 15 and 25: 1, 5, 25 side by side → circle what is in both; both lists start at 1 → the child counts the common factors

point.hi: Yeh 15 ke factors hain: 1, 3, 5, 15. Aur yeh 25 ke factors: 1, 5, 25. Jo number dono liston mein ho, woh 15 aur 25 ka common factor kehlata hai. Dekho, dono listein 1 se shuru hoti hain.
point.en: These are the factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. And these are the factors of 25: 1, 5, 25. A number that is in both lists is called a common factor of 15 and 25. See, both lists start at 1.

prompt.hi: Toh 15 aur 25 ke kitne common factors hain?
prompt.en: So how many common factors do 15 and 25 have?

why.hi: dono liston mein sirf 1 aur 5 hain, yaani 2 common factors
why.en: only 1 and 5 are in both lists, so 2 common factors

simpler.hi: 15 ki list aur 25 ki list saath rakho. Jo number dono mein ho, woh common factor hai, jaise 1.
simpler.en: Put the list for 15 next to the list for 25. A number that is in both is a common factor, like 1.

explain.convey: sharing two things into the same packs → 12 pens went into 3 equal packs of 4 (12 ÷ 3 = 4 over the board) → 3 divides 12; 21 pencils now lie in the same 3 packs unequally (10, 6, 5) and must also share equally → the number of packs has to divide both → a common factor; the child shares the 21 pencils equally

point.hi: Upar likha hai: 12 pens 3 barabar packs mein baante gaye hain, har pack mein 4, kyunki 3 se 12 poora bhaag hota hai. Ab inhi 3 packs mein yeh 21 pencils hain, par abhi 10, 6 aur 5, barabar nahi. Pencils bhi barabar jaani hon, toh packs ki ginti pens aur pencils dono ko poora bhaag kare, yaani woh dono ka common factor ho.
point.en: Written on top: 12 pens are shared into 3 equal packs, 4 in each, because 3 divides 12 exactly. Now these 21 pencils are in the same 3 packs, but as 10, 6 and 5, not equal. If the pencils must go equally too, the number of packs must divide both the pens and the pencils exactly, that is, it must be a common factor of both.

prompt.hi: Inhi 3 packs mein 21 pencils bhi barabar daalo. Har pack mein kitni pencils jaayengi?
prompt.en: Put 21 pencils equally into these same 3 packs too. How many pencils go in each pack?

why.hi: 21 ÷ 3 = 7, aur ek bhi pencil nahi bachti
why.en: 21 ÷ 3 = 7, with not one pencil left over

simpler.hi: 12 pens 3 packs mein 4-4 gaye, kuch nahi bacha. Pencils bhi inhi packs mein jaayein, toh packs ki ginti dono ko poora bhaag de.
simpler.en: The 12 pens went 4 to each of 3 packs, none left. If pencils go in the same packs, the number of packs must divide both exactly.

problem.en: Find the common factors of 20 and 30.

simpler.hi: Pehle 20 ke factors likho, phir 30 ke. Jo number dono list mein ho, woh common factor hai.
simpler.en: First write the factors of 20, then of 30. A number in both lists is a common factor.

find.hi: woh factors jo 20 aur 30 dono ke hain
find.en: the factors that belong to both 20 and 30

do.hi: 20 ki factor ki jodiyan 1 se shuru karke likho
do.en: Write the factor pairs of 20, starting from 1

why.hi: har jodi ke dono numbers 20 ko poora bhaag karte hain
why.en: both numbers of every pair divide 20 exactly

simpler.hi: 20 ko 1 se shuru karke bhaag do aur jodiyan likho, jaise 2 × 10. Har jodi ke dono numbers 20 ke factor hain.
simpler.en: Divide 20 starting from 1 and write the pairs, like 2 × 10. Both numbers of each pair are factors of 20.

do.hi: 30 ki factor ki jodiyan bhi 1 se shuru karke likho
do.en: Write the factor pairs of 30 too, starting from 1

why.hi: har jodi ke dono numbers 30 ko poora bhaag karte hain
why.en: both numbers of every pair divide 30 exactly

simpler.hi: 30 ki jodiyan bhi 1 se shuru karo, jaise 3 × 10 aur 5 × 6. Har jodi ke dono numbers 30 ke factor hain.
simpler.en: Start the pairs of 30 from 1 too, like 3 × 10 and 5 × 6. Both numbers of each pair are factors of 30.

prompt.hi: Ab dono liston ko milao. Kaunse numbers dono liston mein aate hain?
prompt.en: Now match the two lists. Which numbers are in both lists?

simpler.hi: 20 wali list ka har number lo. Dekho woh 30 wali list mein bhi hai ya nahi.
simpler.en: Take each number in the list for 20. See whether it is also in the list for 30.

why.hi: dono jodiyan dekho: 1, 2, 5 aur 10 dono liston mein hain, yeh 20 aur 30 dono ko poora bhaag karte hain
why.en: 1, 2, 5 and 10 are in both lists; they divide both 20 and 30 exactly

answer.hi: 20 aur 30 ke common factors 1, 2, 5 aur 10 hain, aur inme sabse bada 10 hai
answer.en: the common factors of 20 and 30 are 1, 2, 5 and 10, and the biggest of them is 10

why.hi: yahi numbers dono liston mein hain, yaani yeh 20 ko bhi poora bhaag karte hain aur 30 ko bhi
why.en: these are the numbers in both lists, so they divide 20 exactly and 30 exactly too

prompt.hi: {friend} kehta hai ki 12 aur 35 ka koi bhi common factor nahi hai, kyunki 12 = 3 × 4 aur 35 = 5 × 7. {friend} ne kaunsa common factor chhod diya?
prompt.en: {friend} says 12 and 35 have no common factor at all, because 12 = 3 × 4 and 35 = 5 × 7. Which common factor did {friend} leave out?

why.hi: 12 = 1 × 12 aur 35 = 1 × 35 bhi hain, toh 1 dono ka common factor hai
why.en: 12 = 1 × 12 and 35 = 1 × 35 too, so 1 is a common factor of both

simpler.hi: 12 aur 35, dono ki sabse pehli factor ki jodi dekho. Dono jodiyon mein ek number same hai.
simpler.en: Look at the very first factor pair of 12 and of 35. One number is the same in both pairs.

prompt.hi: Inmein se kaunsa number 18 ko bhi aur 27 ko bhi poora bhaag karta hai: 9 ya 54?
prompt.en: Which of these divides both 18 and 27 exactly: 9 or 54?

why.hi: 18 ÷ 9 = 2 aur 27 ÷ 9 = 3; 54 toh dono ka common multiple hai, factor nahi
why.en: 18 ÷ 9 = 2 and 27 ÷ 9 = 3; 54 is a common multiple of both, not a factor

simpler.hi: Jo number dono ko poora bhaag kare, woh dono se bada nahi ho sakta. Ab dekho 54, 18 se bada hai ya chhota.
simpler.en: A number that divides both exactly cannot be bigger than them. Now see whether 54 is bigger or smaller than 18.

simpler.en: Every factor list's first pair is 1 times the number, so both lists start with the same number. Then match the numbers further along too.

prompt.hi: Pehla number 6 hai aur doosra number 9. Dono ke kitne common factors hain?
prompt.en: The first number is 6 and the second number is 9. How many common factors do they have?

why.hi: 6 ke factors 1, 2, 3, 6 aur 9 ke 1, 3, 9; dono mein 1 aur 3, yaani 2
why.en: 6 has factors 1, 2, 3, 6 and 9 has 1, 3, 9; 1 and 3 are in both, so 2

simpler.en: Write the factors of 6, then the factors of 9. Count the numbers that are in both lists.

remediation.move: sharing makes groups SMALLER than the amounts → the number of plates divides both amounts → a common factor; a common multiple is at least as big as the bigger amount, so there would not be enough things to fill that many plates

say.hi: Barabar baantne mein plates ki ginti dono cheezon ko poora bhaag karti hai, yaani woh common factor hai. Common multiple toh dono mein se bade number jitna ya usse bhi bada hota hai, utni plates bharne ke liye cheezein hi nahi hongi.
say.en: When sharing equally, the number of plates divides both things exactly, so it is a common factor. A common multiple is at least as big as the bigger of the two numbers, and there would not even be enough things to fill that many plates.

simpler.hi: Plates ki ginti dono cheezon ko poora bhaag karti hai, isliye woh common factor hai. Common multiple dono mein se bade number jitna ya usse bada hota hai, utni cheezein hi nahi hongi.
simpler.en: The number of plates divides both things exactly, so it is a common factor. A common multiple is at least as big as the bigger number; there are not that many things.

prompt.hi: 14 pens aur 21 pencils ke ek jaise packs banane hain, kuch na bache. Sabse zyada kitne packs?
prompt.en: 14 pens and 21 pencils go into identical packs, nothing left over. What is the most packs?

why.hi: 7 dono ko poora bhaag karta hai, 14 ÷ 7 = 2, 21 ÷ 7 = 3; isse bada common factor nahi
why.en: 7 divides both exactly, 14 ÷ 7 = 2 and 21 ÷ 7 = 3, and no common factor is bigger

simpler.hi: Packs ki ginti 14 aur 21 dono ko poora bhaag de. Dono ke common factors mein sabse bada chuno.
simpler.en: The number of packs must divide both 14 and 21 exactly. Pick the biggest of their common factors.

bridgeToNext.hi: Common factors baantne mein kaam aate hain. Agle hisse mein multiples ki baari hai: jab do cheezein baar-baar hoti hain, toh woh saath kab hoti hain.
bridgeToNext.en: Common factors help in sharing. In the next part it is the turn of multiples: when two things keep happening again and again, when do they happen together.

simpler.hi: Ab multiples ki baari hai. Board par 3 aur 5 ke multiples ki listein hain.
simpler.en: Now it is the turn of multiples. On the board are the multiples lists of 3 and 5.

hook.convey: two things repeating at different gaps (a game's calls, two beats, two buses) meet only at numbers in both times tables → common multiples; the first meeting is often before the product

use.hi: Idli-vada game mein sab baari-baari number bolte hain. 3 ke multiple par 'idli', 5 ke multiple par 'vada', aur jo number dono ka multiple ho, us par 'idli-vada'.
use.en: In the idli-vada game everyone says numbers in turn. On a multiple of 3 you say 'idli', on a multiple of 5 'vada', and on a number that is a multiple of both, 'idli-vada'.

use.hi: Music class mein drum har 2 beat par bajta hai aur taali har 3 beat par. Dono 6, 12, 18 beat par saath aate hain, yeh 2 aur 3 ke common multiples hain.
use.en: In music class the drum plays every 2 beats and the clap comes every 3 beats. Both come together on beats 6, 12, 18; these are common multiples of 2 and 3.

use.hi: Ek bus stop par do buses alag-alag gap par aati hain. Dono phir se ek saath kab aayengi, yeh unke gaps ke common multiple se pata chalta hai.
use.en: Two buses come to a bus stop at different gaps. When they will next come together is found from a common multiple of their gaps.

explain.convey: common multiple = in the multiples list of both numbers → idli-vada with 3 and 5: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 and 5, 10, 15 → 15 is in both → 'idli-vada'; the game goes on → the child decides what to say at a number in only one table

point.hi: 3 ke multiples 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 par 'idli' bolte hain, aur 5 ke multiples 5, 10, 15 par 'vada'. 15 dono liston mein hai, isliye 15 par 'idli-vada'. 15, 3 aur 5 ka common multiple hai.
point.en: On the multiples of 3, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, we say 'idli', and on the multiples of 5, 5, 10, 15, 'vada'. 15 is in both lists, so at 15 it is 'idli-vada'. 15 is a common multiple of 3 and 5.

prompt.hi: Game aage chalta raha. 20 par kya bologe: idli, vada ya idli-vada?
prompt.en: The game goes on. What do you say at 20: idli, vada or idli-vada?

why.hi: 20 = 5 × 4, toh 20 5 ke pahade mein hai, par 3 ke pahade mein nahi; isliye sirf 'vada'
why.en: 20 = 5 × 4 is in the 5 times table but not in the 3 times table, so just 'vada'

simpler.hi: Pehle dekho 20 kis pahade mein aata hai: 3 ke, 5 ke, ya dono ke. Phir game ka niyam lagao.
simpler.en: First see which times table 20 is in: the 3 table, the 5 table, or both. Then apply the game's rule.

explain.convey: the first common multiple is not always the product → 6 and 8: 6 × 8 = 48, but lists 6, 12, 18 … and 8, 16 … meet earlier → extend both lists and stop at the first number in both

point.hi: 6 ke multiples 6, 12, 18 se shuru hote hain aur 8 ke multiples 8, 16 se. 6 × 8 = 48 zaroor ek common multiple hai, par pehla common multiple hamesha guna wala number nahi hota. Dono listein aage badhao aur dekho pehli baar kahan milti hain.
point.en: The multiples of 6 start 6, 12, 18 and the multiples of 8 start 8, 16. 6 × 8 = 48 is surely a common multiple, but the first common multiple is not always the product. Extend both lists and see where they first meet.

prompt.hi: Dono listein aage badhao. 6 aur 8 ka pehla common multiple kya hai?
prompt.en: Extend both lists. What is the first common multiple of 6 and 8?

why.hi: 24 = 6 × 4 = 8 × 3 hai; 8, 16 ke baad 24 aata hai, isse chhota koi saajha nahi
why.en: 24 = 6 × 4 = 8 × 3; after 8, 16 comes 24, and no smaller number is in both tables

simpler.hi: 6 aur 8 ke multiples ki listein aage likhte jao. Jahan dono mein pehli baar ek hi number aaye, wahi pehla common multiple hai.
simpler.en: Keep writing the lists of multiples of 6 and 8. Where the same number first shows up in both, that is the first common multiple.

explain.convey: word problems: things that repeat and meet again (lights, bells, buses) → common multiples, the first one for 'next time together'; sharing into equal groups → common factors; two lights every 4 s and every 14 s → the child finds when they flash together again

point.hi: Light A har 4 second par jalti hai aur light B har 14 second par. Yeh baar-baar dohraana hai, isliye dono ke saath jalne wale pal 4 aur 14 ke common multiples par aate hain. Agli baar saath kab, iske liye pehla common multiple chahiye. Barabar baantne wale sawaal mein common factor lagta hai.
point.en: Light A flashes every 4 seconds and light B every 14 seconds. This is repeating again and again, so the moments they flash together come at the common multiples of 4 and 14. For 'together when next', we need the first common multiple. A question about sharing equally would need a common factor.

prompt.hi: Dono lights abhi saath jali. Kitne second baad phir saath jalengi?
prompt.en: Both lights just flashed together. After how many seconds will they flash together again?

why.hi: light A har 4 second, light B har 14 second jalti hai; dono pehli baar 28 par milti hain
why.en: light A flashes every 4 seconds, light B every 14, and both come together first at 28

simpler.hi: Light A 4 ke pahade par jalti hai, light B 14 ke pahade par. Dono saath tab jalengi jab second dono pahadon mein ho.
simpler.en: Light A flashes on the 4 times table, light B on the 14 times table. They flash together when the second is in both tables.

problem.hi: Kavya apne tulsi ke paudhe ko har 6 din par paani deti hai aur fish bowl har 9 din par saaf karti hai. Aaj usne dono kaam kiye. Kitne din baad woh phir dono kaam ek hi din karegi, aur ismein common factors lagenge ya common multiples?
problem.en: Kavya waters her tulsi plant every 6 days and cleans the fish bowl every 9 days. She did both jobs today. After how many days will she next do both jobs on the same day, and does this need common factors or common multiples?

simpler.hi: Kavya tulsi ko har 6 din par paani deti hai aur fish bowl har 9 din par saaf karti hai. Aaj usne dono kaam kiye. Dekhna hai ki dono kaam phir ek hi din kab honge.
simpler.en: Kavya waters the tulsi every 6 days and cleans the fish bowl every 9 days. She did both jobs today. We need to see when both jobs fall on the same day again.

givens.hi: bowl ki safai har 9 din par

find.hi: aaj ke baad pehla din jab dono kaam saath aayein, aur kaunsa idea lagega
find.en: the first day after today when both jobs fall together, and which idea is needed

do.hi: Dono kaam baar-baar hote hain, toh pehle idea chuno
do.en: Both jobs keep happening again and again, so first choose the idea

why.hi: dono kaam usi din saath aate hain jo dono ke pahade mein ho
why.en: both jobs fall together only on a day that is in both times tables

simpler.hi: Dono kaam baar-baar hote hain. Jo din 6 aur 9 dono ke pahade mein ho, us din dono kaam saath honge.
simpler.en: Both jobs keep happening again and again. On a day that is in both the 6 and 9 times tables, both jobs happen together.

why.hi: paani har 6 din baad diya jaata hai
why.en: the plant is watered every 6 days

simpler.hi: Har 6 din par paani dena hai. Isliye 6 ka pahada likho: 6, 12, 18, aur aage.
simpler.en: The plant is watered every 6 days. So write the 6 times table: 6, 12, 18 and on.

why.hi: bowl har 9 din baad saaf hota hai
why.en: the bowl is cleaned every 9 days

simpler.hi: Bowl har 9 din par saaf hota hai. Isliye 9 ka pahada likho: 9, 18, 27, 36.
simpler.en: The bowl is cleaned every 9 days. So write the 9 times table: 9, 18, 27, 36.

prompt.hi: Dono liston mein sabse pehle kaunsa number aata hai?
prompt.en: Which number comes first in both lists?

simpler.hi: 6 wali list ka har number 9 wali list mein dhoondo. Jo sabse pehle mile, wahi chuno.
simpler.en: Look for each number of the 6 list in the 9 list. Pick the first one you find in both.

why.hi: tulsi ko paani har 6 din, fish bowl har 9 din; 18 dono pahadon mein aane wala pehla din hai
why.en: 18 = 6 × 3 = 9 × 2 is the first number in both lists

answer.hi: Kavya 18 din baad phir dono kaam ek hi din karegi, aur ismein common multiples lagte hain
answer.en: Kavya will next do both jobs on the same day after 18 days, and this needs common multiples

why.hi: dono kaam baar-baar hote hain, toh common multiple chahiye; agli baar yaani pehla, 18, na ki 6 × 9 = 54
why.en: both jobs keep happening, so a common multiple is needed; 'next time' means the first, 18, not 6 × 9 = 54

prompt.hi: Ek bachcha har 6 din par library jaata hai aur doosra har 10 din par. Aaj dono saath gaye. Kitne din baad phir saath jaayenge?
prompt.en: One child goes to the library every 6 days and another every 10 days. Today both went together. After how many days will they go together again?

why.hi: ek bachcha har 6 din, doosra har 10 din jaata hai; 6 aur 10 ke pahade pehli baar 30 par milte hain
why.en: the 6 and 10 times tables first come together at 30

simpler.hi: 6 ka pahada aur 10 ka pahada saath-saath likho. Jahan dono mein pehli baar ek hi number aaye, wahi jawab hai.
simpler.en: Write the 6 and 10 times tables side by side. Where the same number first shows up in both, that is the answer.

prompt.hi: Ek rassi 18 m ki hai aur doosri 30 m ki. Dono ko ek hi lambai ke tukdon mein kaatna hai, kuch na bache. Sabse lamba tukda nikaalne ke liye common factor chahiye ya common multiple?
prompt.en: One rope is 18 m long and another is 30 m. Both are cut into pieces of the same length, with nothing left over. To find the longest piece, do you need a common factor or a common multiple?

why.hi: har rassi barabar tukdon mein baantni hai, toh tukde ki lambai 18 aur 30 dono ko poora bhaag kare: common factor
why.en: each rope is shared into equal pieces, so the piece length must divide both 18 and 30: a common factor

simpler.hi: Tukde ki lambai se dono rassiyan poori kat jaayein. Socho, woh lambai 18 aur 30 ko baantegi ya unke pahade mein aayegi.
simpler.en: The piece length must cut both ropes exactly. Think whether that length divides 18 and 30 or sits in their times tables.

prompt.hi: {friend} kehta hai 6 aur 14 ka pehla common multiple 6 × 14 = 84 hai. Sahi pehla common multiple kya hai?
prompt.en: {friend} says the first common multiple of 6 and 14 is 6 × 14 = 84. What is the real first common multiple?

why.hi: 42 = 6 × 7 = 14 × 3, dono pahadon mein; yeh 84 se pehle aata hai
why.en: 42 = 6 × 7 = 14 × 3 is in both tables, and it comes before 84

simpler.hi: 6 aur 14 ke multiples ki listein aage badhao. Dekho, 84 se pehle hi dono listein kahin milti hain kya.
simpler.en: Extend the lists of multiples of 6 and 14. See whether the two lists meet somewhere before 84.

ladder.why: idli-vada with 3 and 5: test 30, 25, 27 against both tables
predict first: is the first idli-vada for 4 and 6 at 24 → no, at 12
temple bells every 4 and 10 minutes from 9:00 → next together, as a clock time
contrast: buses meeting needs common multiples, equal rows needs common factors
far transfer: app backups every 12 and 18 days → first common multiple, not the product

remediation.move: two frogs hopping from 0 on a number line, one in 8s and one in 10s, leaving footprints → the first shared footprint is 40, well before 8 × 10 = 80 → list and stop at the first match instead of multiplying

say.hi: Do mendhak alag-alag kood lagaate hain toh unki kood ka guna mat karo. Har mendhak ke utarne ki list likho. Dono liston mein jo number pehle aaye, wahin woh milte hain.
say.en: When two frogs hop by different amounts, do not multiply the hops. Write each frog's landings as a list. The first number in both lists is where they meet.

simpler.hi: Har mendhak ke utarne ke number likho. Dono liston ka pehla saajha number hi milne ki jagah hai.
simpler.en: Write the landings of each frog. The first number in both lists is the meeting point.

prompt.hi: Mendhak A har baar 8 aage koodta hai, mendhak B har baar 10, dono 0 se. Pehli baar dono kis number par milenge?
prompt.en: Frog A hops 8 each time, frog B hops 10 each time, both from 0. At which number do they first meet?

why.hi: mendhak A har baar 8, B har baar 10 koodta hai; dono pehli baar 40 par milte hain, 80 par nahi
why.en: frog A hops 8 each time and frog B 10; they first meet at 40, not at 80

simpler.hi: Mendhak A 8 ke pahade par utarta hai, B 10 ke pahade par. Dono listein likho aur pehla saath wala number dhoondo.
simpler.en: Frog A lands on the 8 times table, frog B on the 10 times table. Write both lists and find the first shared number.

remediation.move: read what the question does with the numbers: repeating and meeting again → numbers grow → multiples; sharing into equal groups → groups divide the amounts → factors; then work the sharing case out

say.hi: Jab cheezein baar-baar hoti hain aur poochha jaata hai ki saath kab, toh numbers badhte jaate hain, yeh multiples hain. Jab cheezein barabar baantni hon, toh tokriyon ki ginti amounts ko poora bhaag karti hai, yeh factors hain.
say.en: When things keep happening and the question is when they come together, the numbers keep growing; these are multiples. When things are shared equally, the number of baskets divides the amounts exactly; these are factors.

simpler.hi: Cheezein baar-baar hon aur saath kab poochha jaaye, toh multiples. Cheezein barabar baantni hon, toh tokriyon ki ginti factor hai.
simpler.en: When things keep happening and you ask when they meet, use multiples. When things are shared equally, the number of baskets is a factor.

prompt.hi: 16 aam aur 24 kele ek jaisi tokriyon mein, kuch na bache. Sabse zyada kitni tokriyan banengi?
prompt.en: 16 mangoes and 24 bananas go into identical baskets, nothing left over. What is the most baskets?

why.hi: 8 se 16 aam aur 24 kele poore bant jaate hain, har tokri 2 aam, 3 kele; isse bada common factor nahi
why.en: 8 divides both: 2 mangoes and 3 bananas per basket, and no common factor of 16 and 24 is bigger

simpler.hi: Tokriyon ki ginti 16 aur 24 dono ko poora bhaag de. Dono ke common factors mein sabse bada chuno.
simpler.en: The number of baskets must divide both 16 and 24 exactly. Pick the biggest of their common factors.
